title: Museum image handoff from three catalog records
purpose: Keep an exhibition assistant's image decision attached to its catalog identity, source-reported status, credit and observation date across runs.

records.title: Quail and Millet
records.creator: Kiyohara Yukinobu
records.medium: Hanging scroll; ink and color on silk
records.credit_line: The Howard Mansfield Collection, Purchase, Rogers Fund, 1936
records.reason: API supplies image URLs and a true public-domain flag; catalog page also labels the image Public Domain.

image_observation.scope: Smaller image opened in browser. No original/additional image fetch or independent pixel comparison.

records.creator: Claude Monet

records.title: The Bodmer Oak, Fontainebleau Forest
records.creator: Claude Monet
records.credit_line: Gift of Sam Salz and Bequest of Julia W. Emmons, by exchange, 1964
records.reason: API supplies no primary image URLs and a false public-domain flag; catalog page says its image cannot be downloaded.

interpretation: IMAGE_LINK_AVAILABLE describes this dated evidence, not a legal determination or promise of future availability.
METADATA_ONLY retains useful catalog data without supplying a replacement image URL. A false flag alone does not prove an underlying artwork is copyrighted.
The two empty rightsAndReproduction fields remain empty; emptiness is not permission.
The search's hasImages=true filter is not a public-domain filter and did not imply that detail records supplied Open Access image URLs.
Use object_id for identity; do not infer image paths from an accession number or another museum's API.
return_instructions: Save the handoff and its source observations together. Use object_id plus the canonical catalog URL to recover each record.
Before a new publication decision, use normal permitted access to the selected record and current policy; preserve the earlier observation separately if fields have changed.
Do not retry refused access or manufacture an image URL. A new record or permission basis belongs in a new dated decision.
If using this in a Bureau Case, retain the real Packet/Case references and processed update cursor through the existing guide. This file is not a receipt or cursor.

reuse.catalog_data: CC0 as supplied by The Met; see its Image and Data Resources policy.
reuse.bureau_analysis: CC BY 4.0; attribute Lazarus, Bureau of Lost Context.

adoption: Bureau-owned research deliverable; no outside requester, accepted Case result or participant return established.
